data.raw_text:
From the one-room schoolhouses of Roane County, West Virginia, Ruby Bradley traded her chalkboard for a uniform—and became a legend.

Born near Spencer in 1907, she taught school before becoming a nurse and joining the Army Nurse Corps in 1934.

Captured in WWII Philippines, she spent 3 years as a POW, assisting in surgeries, delivering babies, and smuggling food to starving children—earning the nickname "Angel in Fatigues." She emerged weighing just 86 lbs but never stopped serving.

In Korea, she saved lives under fire. Retired as Colonel in 1963 with 34 decorations—the most decorated woman in U.S. military history.

A true Mountain State hero.
